findings.evidence: Worked schemas then paste two full blog and social-network schemas (USER, POST, COMMENT, CATEGORY, TAG, POST_TAG, LIKE, FOLLOW, MESSAGE, NOTIFICATION, CHAT_GROUP, GROUP_MEMBER), about 230 of the file's 400 lines, after steps 1-8 already decide naming, parent/child glyphs, identifying lines and junctions.
findings.fix: Keep one compact worked schema that exercises a composite-key junction, a nullable self-reference and a polymorphic column. Move the second full schema to a short pointer (the steps already produce it) or record the cut in docs/audit/recovery/mermaid-diagrams/record.md; do not delete the cardinality rules.

findings.evidence: Section 6 says palette A is the default, then 'Pick another block only by what the colors mean: A for architecture or service maps, B when the diagram shows status, C for before/after.' A status or before/after flowchart has two equal instructions.
findings.fix: Make the default conditional: status meanings use palette B, before/after uses C, and A is the default only when the colors mean structure or services. Leave the hex blocks unchanged.

findings.evidence: Step 4 says 'for a new diagram, split it if it fails' the section 2 size check, but authoring-rules.md section 2 says 'Split only when text becomes unreadable at the target column width (about 900px) or the diagram grows taller than about three screens' and a height/width below 0.4 is only a warning sign.
findings.fix: In SKILL.md step 4, split a new diagram only when the rendered text is unreadable at about 900px or the diagram is taller than about three screens; keep a short wide diagram whose text stays readable, and still only report (do not restructure) a repair.
